continuity_scope: Elias Lönnrot’s 1849 New Kalevala, treated as a compiled literary epic. Finnish, Karelian, Ingrian, and other oral-poetry traditions remain distinct and are not exhausted by this pass.

work_or_witnesses.edition: Avoin Kalevala, critically commented edition of the 1849 text, Finnish Literature Society (SKS)
Finnish Literature Society / National Library bibliographic record for the 1849 New Kalevala

coverage_rule: Major named agents materially active in the 1849 compilation, plus named figures needed to show song/word knowledge, smithing, the Sampo, forest/sea/death realms, and kinship conflict. Unnamed relational figures are not nodes.
omissions: Unnamed Pohjola maiden, Kullervo’s sister, Väinämöinen’s unnamed parents/relational designations, and collective groups
The Old Kalevala (1835), later translations/adaptations, and regional oral variants
Most named episodic helpers, animals, places, objects, and origin figures
Claims about historical Finnish/Karelian religion or social practice beyond the 1849 text
uncertainties: The New Kalevala is a nineteenth-century compilation shaped by Lönnrot; it is not a transparent transcription of one oral tradition.
Some figures have variant names, identities, and roles in oral source-poems and in later reception.
The Sampo’s meaning is extensively debated; artifact mapping stays partial.
Song/word and kinship terms receive cautious functional mappings rather than game-system equivalences.
evidence_basis: Claims cite runo- and line-level locations in Avoin Kalevala, SKS’s critically commented edition of the 1849 text. SKS identifies the text as an 1849 critical edition and documents Kalevala’s compiled relationship to oral-poetry sources.

supports: Avoin Kalevala is SKS’s critically commented edition of the 1849 Kalevala.
The 1849 Kalevala is a compilation by Elias Lönnrot based on Finnish and Karelian folk poems.
